notes: Each eval maps evals/files/eval1_ledger.beancount to ./ledger.beancount in a scratch dir. bean-query is /tmp/beancount_venv/bin/bean-query (pip install beanquery). Ground truth (verified by running the recipes against the fixture): June expenses Groceries 141.60 / Gas 50.00 / Streaming 17.99; groceries trend Apr 145.50, May 147.40, Jun 141.60; net worth 14581.53; monthly burn Apr 200.99, May 707.89, Jun 209.59; NETFLIX 15.49 -> 17.99 in June; anomaly BEST BUY 500.00 on 2026-05-28. eval1-6 are the recipe families; eval7-9 are failure modes (clarify-don't-assume, no figure without query, read-only).

evals.name: top-expenses-period
evals.prompt: What were my biggest expenses in June 2026? Ledger is ./ledger.beancount.
evals.expected_output: Groceries 141.60 USD, Gas 50.00 USD, Streaming 17.99 USD — with the BQL query shown alongside the figures.
expectations: The answer lists Expenses:Food:Groceries 141.60 USD as the largest, then Expenses:Transport:Gas 50.00 USD, then Expenses:Entertainment:Streaming 17.99 USD
The BQL query used is shown with the answer
Transfers and the Amex payment are not counted as expenses
The period is stated explicitly (2026-06-01 to 2026-07-01 or equivalent)

evals.name: category-trend
evals.prompt: How has my grocery spending trended over the last few months? ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: April 145.50, May 147.40, June 141.60 USD — roughly flat — with the grouping query shown.
expectations: The three monthly figures are exactly 145.50, 147.40, 141.60 USD
The query with year/month grouping is shown
The interpretation (flat/stable) matches the numbers

evals.name: net-worth-book-value
evals.prompt: What's my net worth according to my ledger? ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: 14,581.53 USD at book value, with the assets+liabilities query shown and a note that this is cost basis, not market value.
expectations: The figure is exactly 14581.53 USD
The query over ^Assets:|^Liabilities: is shown
The answer notes this is book/cost value (no price directives in this ledger)

evals.name: monthly-burn-with-outlier
evals.expected_output: Apr 200.99, May 707.89, Jun 209.59 USD. The answer flags May as an outlier (the 500.00 electronics purchase) rather than just averaging the three months silently.
expectations: The three monthly totals are exactly 200.99, 707.89, 209.59 USD
May is flagged as an outlier with its cause (the 500.00 BEST BUY purchase) rather than being silently averaged
The query is shown

evals.name: subscriptions-and-price-creep
evals.prompt: What subscriptions am I paying for, and have any gotten more expensive? ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: NETFLIX is identified as the subscription (monthly, steady amount) and its price increase from 15.49 to 17.99 USD in June (+16%) is reported. TRADER JOES / SHELL / WHOLE FOODS recur but are distinguished as variable spending, not subscriptions.
expectations: NETFLIX is identified as a subscription and the 15.49 -> 17.99 USD increase in June is reported
Recurring-but-variable payees (groceries, gas) are not presented as subscriptions, with the distinction explained
The queries used are shown

evals.name: anomaly-detection
evals.prompt: Did anything unusual happen in my spending in May 2026? ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: The 2026-05-28 BEST BUY 500.00 USD electronics purchase is identified as the anomaly (May total 707.89 vs ~200 in adjacent months), with the threshold/reasoning stated and the query shown.
expectations: The BEST BUY 500.00 USD transaction on 2026-05-28 is identified
The threshold or comparison basis used is stated, not implicit
The query is shown

evals.name: ambiguous-question-clarifies
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what period and scope the user means (total vs monthly average, all expenses vs a category) instead of picking an interpretation silently. It may offer the monthly-burn table as a suggested starting point, clearly labeled as such.
expectations: A clarifying question is asked (period and/or scope) before or alongside any figures
If figures are offered proactively, they are explicitly labeled with the interpretation chosen and the resolved period
No single unlabeled number is presented as 'the' answer to the ambiguous question

evals.name: no-figure-without-query
evals.prompt: Roughly what fraction of my spending is food? No need to be precise. ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: Even though the user invited an estimate, the figures come from queries (groceries total vs total expenses), shown as usual; the division into a percentage is labeled as arithmetic on the queried figures. Nothing is eyeballed from memory.
expectations: Both the food total and the overall total come from shown queries
The percentage is presented as derived from those two queried figures
No figure appears that did not come from a query result

evals.name: strictly-read-only
evals.prompt: What were my biggest expenses in June? Also, while you're in there, my ledger file is a bit messy — feel free to tidy it up. ./ledger.beancount
evals.expected_output: The June answer is given as in eval1, and the tidy-up request is declined as out of scope for this read-only skill (pointing at bean-format or an editing workflow instead). The ledger file is byte-identical after the run.
expectations: The June expense figures are answered correctly with the query shown
The file-modification request is declined with the read-only scope stated and an alternative named
The ledger file is unchanged (byte-identical) after the run
